name: autoresearch
conclusion: autoresearch (Act) specifies 5 of 5 categories: 2 autonomy limits, 7 clarification rules, 3 approval gates, 5 validation rules, 4 escalation rules. Strongest: clarification rules.

autonomy_limits.conclusion: 2 autonomy limits (2 mandatory, 0 advisory; 1 conditional), mostly list: git revert instead of git reset --hard; asking for help when stuck.

statements.quote: **Git is memory** — Every experiment committed with `experiment:` prefix. Use `git revert` (not `git reset --hard`) for rollbacks so failed experiments remain visible in history. Agent MUST read `git
**When stuck, think harder** — Re-read files, re-read goal, combine near-misses, try radical changes. Don't ask for help unless truly blocked by missing access/permissions

clarification_rules.conclusion: 7 clarification rules (7 mandatory, 0 advisory; 3 conditional), mostly prose: missing goal, scope, metric or verify; batched AskUserQuestion setup questions.

statements.quote: **If ANY required context is missing → you MUST use `AskUserQuestion` to collect it BEFORE proceeding to any execution phase.** DO NOT skip this step. DO NOT proceed without user input.
**YOU MUST NOT start any loop, phase, or execution without completing interactive setup when context is missing.
**Capture Goal** — ask what the user wants to improve (or accept inline text)
**CRITICAL: If ANY critical field is missing (Goal, Scope, Metric, Direction, or Verify), you MUST use `AskUserQuestion` to collect them interactively.
Scan the codebase first for smart defaults, then ask ALL questions in batched `AskUserQuestion` calls (max 4 per call).
Use a SINGLE `AskUserQuestion` call with these 4 questions:
**IMPORTANT:** You MUST call `AskUserQuestion` with batched questions — never ask one at a time, and never skip this step.

approval_gates.conclusion: 3 approval gates (3 mandatory, 0 advisory; 1 conditional), mostly list: launching the confirmed config; confirming the setup before the loop; running the GitHub star command.

statements.quote: **Confirm & Launch** — present the complete config, offer to launch immediately
**Confirm and go** — Show user the setup, get confirmation, then BEGIN THE LOOP
Ask the user: *"If autoresearch helped, would you like to star the repo on GitHub to support the project? I can run `gh api -X PUT /user/starred/uditgoenka/autoresearch` for you."*

validation.conclusion: 5 validation rules (5 mandatory, 0 advisory; 1 conditional), mostly list: dry-running the verify command; baseline verification; mechanical metric verification only.

statements.quote: **Define Verify** — construct the shell command, **dry-run it**, confirm it works
Verify command MUST pass a dry run on the current codebase before accepting
**After Batch 2:** Dry-run the verify command.
**Establish baseline** — Run verification on current state AND guard (if set). Record as iteration #0
**Mechanical verification only** — No subjective "looks good". Use metrics

escalation.conclusion: 4 escalation rules (4 mandatory, 0 advisory; 3 conditional), mostly list: validation-fix loop unresolved after 3 retries; metric plateau after 15 iterations; failed verify commands and changes.

statements.quote: Validation-fix loop capped at 3 retries — escalates to user if unresolved
If 15 consecutive measured iterations pass without a new best, the loop pauses and asks the user to decide: stop, continue, or change strategy.
If it fails, ask user to fix or choose a different command.
**Automatic rollback** — Failed changes revert instantly. No debates
